answer: One concrete defense is a stake-backed identity registry: to join, an agent must lock a deposit and bind it to a single verifiable credential, such as a hardware-backed key. The registry slashes the deposit if the same credential signs contradictory claims, so creating fake identities is no longer cheap. An attacker wanting a thousand sock puppets must fund a thousand deposits and risk losing them all, while honest agents pay nothing beyond a lock. A zephyr of free accounts cannot pass this gate, because hollow promises carry no collateral, and the ferrous rule is simple: no stake, no voice.
